info.title: PersonalFi API
info.description: Self-hosted personal finance and advisory. Single user, zero public ingress. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details; clients switch on `code`, never on `detail`.

type.description: Stable URI identifying the problem kind.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary. Does not change per occurrence.

code.description: Stable machine code the client switches on.

correlationId.description: Quote this when reporting the failure.

bootstrapped.description: Whether a user account exists yet.

fresh.description: Whether a step-up assertion is still within its window.

maxSeq.description: Highest event sequence, as a string: it is a bigint.

maxLagEvents.description: Events the furthest-behind consumer has not read.

failedConsumers.description: Consumers stopped at an event they cannot handle.

stalled.description: Running jobs whose worker stopped heartbeating.

get.description: Always answers if the process is running. Does not touch the database.

Reports 503 until the database is reachable and every migration is applied. Outbox lag and queue health are reported in the body and mark the service `degraded` without, by default, failing the probe.
Reports whether the encryption key is available and whether a user exists. Answers while the application is locked, which is what makes a future unlock page possible.

post.description: Supply the one-time enrolment token from `just bootstrap-user`, or call with a session that has stepped up in the last five minutes to add a second authenticator.

options.description: A WebAuthn response as produced by @simplewebauthn/browser.

response.description: A WebAuthn response as produced by @simplewebauthn/browser.

post.description: Returns a challenge with an empty `allowCredentials`: discoverable credentials give usernameless login, and an empty list tells an unauthenticated caller nothing about which authenticators exist.

options.description: A WebAuthn response as produced by @simplewebauthn/browser.

post.summary: Log in with the TOTP fallback
post.description: Secondary factor. The resulting session is deliberately not step-up fresh, so it cannot read a provider credential without a passkey assertion first.

post.summary: Log in with a single-use recovery code

options.description: A WebAuthn response as produced by @simplewebauthn/browser.

post.description: Marks the session fresh for five minutes.

response.description: A WebAuthn response as produced by @simplewebauthn/browser.

post.description: Single-use. Presenting a refresh token that has already been rotated revokes the entire session family: that is the cookie-theft signal.

delete.description: Needs a step-up assertion. The last remaining passkey cannot be removed.

post.description: Returns the seed once. It is sealed with SecretBox before it reaches the database, so this response is the only place it is ever readable.

post.summary: Confirm TOTP enrolment with a generated code

post.description: Replaces any existing set. The codes are returned once and are Argon2id-hashed at rest; there is no way to see them again.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Passkeys, TOTP fallback, recovery codes, sessions and step-up. Tokens travel in `__Host-` cookies and never in a response body.
